Photograph: Pedro Salado/Getty Images Luke McLaughlin Tue 3 Nov 2026 15.24 EST First published on Tue 3 Nov 2026 13.30 EST Share Key events 14m ago Goal: 7 min: Barcelona 1-0 Aston Villa (Lamine Yamal) 
 22m ago First half kick-off

 1m ago 15.23 EST 20 min: Villa counter down the right, and quickly. Manzambi plays Jackson in, and he’s in acres of space due to Barcelona’s high line: the forward suddenly has just the goalie to beat! But García comes way, way out of his area and puts in a vital tackle.
 Share Updated at  15.24 EST 3m ago 15.22 EST 19 min: Another chance for Villa! Manzambi meets a square ball from Jackson, from the Villa right, but he scuffs it horribly! McGinn did well to step over the ball and leave it for Manzambi there.
 Share 5m ago 15.20 EST 16 min: A dangerous run by Gordon down the hosts’ left. He squares the ball low but neither Raphinha nor Lamine Yamal can meet the cross with an effort on goal.
 They replay the goal on telly: Lamine Yamal was exceptionally alert to the possibility of Joan García playing the horrible pass that he did after the pass out from Suzuki. It was so naive from Villa. And Emery will be disgusted to have conceded such a soft goal. Still, there is still hope …
 Share Updated at  15.20 EST 8m ago 15.17 EST 14 min: McGinn pumps a ball down into the left channel looking for the run of Jackson. Joan García, the goalie, plays sweeper and deals with it easily. Still, Villa don’t look intimidated, even if they’ve handed Barcelona a one-goal lead on a silver platter.
 Share Updated at  15.17 EST 9m ago 15.15 EST 13 min: Lamine Yamal sprints to the byline again with the ball under his command. But then, the ball sneaks out for a goal kick before he squares it.
 Oh, he is human!
 Share 11m ago 15.14 EST 11 min: Maatsen goes in the book after Lamine Yamal mugs him off, touching the ball past the Villa defender, and going to ground. Now a nervy disciplinary tightrope to walk for the full-back for a mere 80min or so …
 Share Updated at  15.15 EST 12m ago 15.12 EST 9 min: Chances for Villa to hit back immediately! Cash hammers a volley just wide! Another corner – and João Gomes’s point-blank range effort is blocked by Cancelo! That was a brave block by the Barça defender.
 Share Updated at  15.13 EST 13m ago 15.11 EST Villa look to play it out from the back. Suzuki passes to João Gomes, on the edge of the area, who plays a loose first-time pass that is pounced on by Lamine Yamal. The Spain international doesn’t need a second invitation and tucks a simple finish into the bottom corner.
 View image in fullscreen A pinpoint finish from Lamine Yamal givers Barcelona an early lead. Photograph: Pedro Salado/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Barcelona's Lamine Yamal celebrates after scoring the opening goal. Photograph: Joan Monfort/AP Share Updated at  15.18 EST 14m ago 15.10 EST Goal: 7 min: Barcelona 1-0 Aston Villa (Lamine Yamal)
 Oh dear.
 Share 15m ago 15.10 EST 7 min: Raphinha’s set-piece is a low, skiddy one and flashes past the far post. Four or five Barça players may have been offside …
 Share 16m ago 15.09 EST 5 min: Lamine Yamal gets on the ball near the Villa penalty area and is barged into by Buendía. It’s a free-kick in a very handy spot for the home team … the Prince of Wales is pictured up in the stands, keeping a watchful eye on the action. Raphinha will hit the free-kick.
 View image in fullscreen Aston Villa's Emiliano Buendia fouls Barcelona's Lamine Yamal. Photograph: Albert Gea/Reuters Share Updated at  15.13 EST 17m ago 15.07 EST 5 min: López escapes down the Barcelona right and squares for Gordon, whose shot is blocked. Another little warning for Villa …
 Share 19m ago 15.06 EST 3 min: McGinn has his pocket picked in a defensive area, but he gets away with it. He wasn’t alert enough there and Villa won’t be able to afford many lapses like that … Mind you, there shape and composure looks good overall, based on the very early exchanges.
 Share Updated at  15.06 EST 20m ago 15.04 EST 2 min: The 20-year-old Brian Fariñas made his debut for Barcelona at the weekend and keeps his place tonight. I may have said it was three changes for Barça, by the way: it is in fact two – Gerard and Gordon the players coming in.
 Share Updated at  15.04 EST 22m ago 15.02 EST First half kick-off
 Vamos! 
 Share 25m ago 14.59 EST The Champions League anthem will not be played tonight. There will be an opportunity to remember Jesús de Miguel, the Tenerife player who died this week after an on-field collision, as well as the victims of last week’s train crash in Spain .
 Tenerife footballer Jesús de Miguel dies aged 30 after on-pitch collision Read more Share Updated at  15.00 EST 27m ago 14.57 EST Emery’s managerial career record against Barcelona is played 30, won three, lost 21.
 Share 29m ago 14.55 EST It’s hammering down with rain in Barcelona . Well, it is November. It’ll be a nice greasy surface for Villa’s fluid attacking game.
 The players and officials are beginning to assemble in the tunnel.
 View image in fullscreen Emi Buendia (centre left) and Nicolas Jackson warm up. Photograph: Nick Potts/PA View image in fullscreen Some suitably attired Barcelona fans look up for it. Photograph: Nick Potts/PA Share Updated at  15.08 EST 32m ago 14.53 EST We are , quite literally, less than 10 minutes away from kick-off at the Camp Nou.
 There is still time for all you Villa fans to send me your hopes, dreams and fears for this box-office clash in Catalonia.
 Email me.
 Share 39m ago 14.46 EST “ I take 10, 20 minutes every day to sit, visualise, be calm and meditate,” Anthony Gordon tells Jules Breach, in a pre-recorded interview, on TNT Sports.
 “And I am truly grateful for my life, for what I’ve created.”
 Was it always his dream to play abroad? 
 “It seems quite difficult for people to understand that kind of ambition, if you don’t have it yourself … but I think if you speak to any of my family, friends, people who’ve been close to me, I’ve said this from very, very early.
 “Ultimately, now, like most humans – you get to where you want to get to, and then you just want more. I need goals, I need trophies, I need everything else that comes with it.”
 View image in fullscreen Anthony Gordon. Photograph: Alberto Estévez/EPA Share Updated at  14.49 EST 47m ago 14.37 EST Matty Cash v Anthony Gordon, then, on the Barcelona left?
 And Lamine Yamal v Ian Maatsen on the other flank.
 It’s going to be an incredible defensive shift from Villa if they fly back to England with some sort of positive result. You better believe it!
 Share 53m ago 14.32 EST Jules Breach and Gerrard were just having a chat for TNT Sports as the Barcelona players went out to warm up. Gerrard has never seen Lamine Yamal play in the flesh before.
 Anthony Gordon spotted Gerrard and came and said hello. Lamine Yamal then immediately followed suit. Gerrard gave him a slightly awkward hug, and looked genuinely star-struck that the Spain international had come over to say hi. That’s a measure of the young man’s growing reputation right there.
 View image in fullscreen Lamine Yamal. ‘Hola, Stevie G.’ Photograph: Albert Gea/Reuters Share Updated at  14.36 EST 55m ago 14.30 EST “ Good evening ,” says Emery, speaking to TNT Sports. “Yes, we are excited …
 “Today is the highest level in European football. And we are ready … but of course, we know it is going to be a very tough match … but we need to understand how we can compete. How we can exploit our capacity, our skills … and being organised.
 “Barcelona are very, very competitive – favourites in this competition – they have now six points, and playing at home, after defeat against Paris Saint-Germain, they must win – it’s a good test to see how we can compete when the level is high, and when the opponent needs, need to compete against us.”
 Share 1h ago 14.23 EST If you were unfortunate enough to miss Barney Ronay’s excellent preview … here it is again:
 “European football has done a pretty good job in the past two seasons of turning its autumn fixture blizzard into a hopeless and baggy blur. What serious sport actually has a 36-team mega table? And a deeply predictable 36-team mega-table at that, one where you pretty much know who’s going to be up there at the end of it. If the intention was to create a series of exhibition-style TV-product events, thereby heading off the Super League’s desire to do exactly the same, then mission semi-accomplished.
 “There are still exceptions in the period of drift, one-off events that speak to the colour and cultural weight of this competition. Tuesday night is one of them, for Villa’s fans a genuine staging point in the progress of this ever-evolving team, with a chance, dependent on results elsewhere, to actually top the Champions League mega-table at this early stage.”
 Don’t call it a remontada: Emery’s Camp Nou comeback focuses European blur Read more Share 1h ago 14.20 EST Of the four sides who have three wins out of three, it’s PSG and Villa in action today. Liverpool and Real Madrid both play tomorrow.

 Share 1h ago 14.12 EST Steven Gerrard and Ally McCoist are on co-commentary duty for TNT Sports alongside Darren Fletcher in Barcelona . The sight and sound of Gerrard has reminded me to recap CarragherGate:
 “ Jamie Carragher has apologised to Aston Villa for using “clumsy and wrong” language when discussing the club, after club had threatened legal action. “I’d like to apologise to Aston Villa , the owners and their fans. My language this week was clumsy and wrong,” Carragher wrote on X on Saturday.
 “I can assure Villa fans it was tongue-in-cheek but I can understand it’s not come across that way, so apologies. Good luck today UTV [Up the Villa]!”
 Jamie Carragher apologises to Aston Villa for ‘clumsy and wrong’ comments Read more “ Aston Villa have dropped their threat of legal action against Jamie Carragher following an apology from the Sky Sports pundit.
 “Villa announced on Friday that they would be taking legal action against Carragher for “unacceptable insults about the club and its fans” on the Stick to Football podcast. The former Liverpool defender had told Villa supporters to “shut the fuck up” after being criticised for suggesting Unai Emery should consider taking the Manchester United job if Michael Carrick is sacked.”
 Aston Villa drop threat of legal action against Jamie Carragher after apology Read more Share Updated at  14.13 EST 1h ago 14.08 EST Will Unwin is blogging crisis club Manchester United v Roma here:
 Manchester United v Roma: Champions League – live Read more Share 1h ago 13.58 EST Teams
 Emery makes two changes to the side that drew 1-1 with Fulham on Saturday: João Gomes into midfield, for Leon Goretzka, and Emi Buendía comes into the forward line, replacing Alysson.
 Also two changes from Barcelona’s Hansi Flick: he brings in Gerard in central defence, for Frenkie de Jong, and Anthony Gordon for Karim Adeyemi up front.
 Barcelona (4-2-3-1) : Joan García; Fariñas, Cubarsi, Gerard, Cancelo; Rodri, Gonzalez; Yamal, López, Gordon; Raphinha. Subtitutes : Szczesny, Livakovic, Balde, Gavi, Gabriel Jesus, Adeyemi, de Jong, Bernal, Abdelkarim, Goren, Victor, Campos.
 Aston Villa (4-2-3-1): Suzuki; Cash, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen; Kamara, João Gomes; McGinn, Manzambi, Buendia; Jackson. Subtitutes : Bizot, Wright, Harwood-Bellis, Mings, Barkley, Garnacho, Abraham, Mbaye, Goretzka, Alysson, Hemmings.
 Referee: Davide Massa (Italy)

 Share 2h ago 13.50 EST Any other Villa fans in this evening?
 Email me.
 Share 2h ago 13.49 EST Some Villa fans , earlier, lapping up the atmosphere in Barcelona .
 Dos cervezas por favor. 
 View image in fullscreen Aston Villa supporters in Spain. Photograph: Nick Potts/PA And some Spanish-themed Villains here:
 View image in fullscreen Aston Villa fans dressed up in Spanish clobber. Photograph: Manjit Narotra/ProSports/Shutterstock Share Updated at  13.50 EST 2h ago 13.46 EST “ Very fortunate to be at the game tonight,” emails Dave. “The stadium and facilities around it are more like the NFL. It’s a brilliant experience.
 “Villa smash and grab, sit deep and get them on the break. Ride the luck in the last 20 and get it launched.”
 Brilliant – thanks for your email Dave – enjoy the occasion and good luck.
 View image in fullscreen Merchandise for sale near the Camp Nou. Photograph: Nick Potts/PA Share Updated at  13.46 EST 2h ago 13.42 EST Barney Ronay “One more match . Just one more match.” Sure, Unai. Sure. Just like all the other matches that generated a local tremor measured at 1 on the Richter scale when that seventh and final goal went in at the Camp Nou in March 2017.
 “It was inevitable that Unai Emery would be asked about the Remontada game on the eve of Aston Villa’s Champions League engagement with Barcelona, his own first trip back to the Camp Nou in this competition since one of the most visceral and traumatic experiences of his managerial career.
 “Emery was Paris Saint-Germain’s manager the night the Neymar-Messi-Suárez triple-godhead reversed a 4-0 first-leg quarter-final deficit in this stadium.
 Don’t call it a remontada: Emery’s Camp Nou comeback focuses European blur Read more Share 2h ago 13.36 EST Speaking of Barcelona and subtext:
 “Plays, novels, songs. They all have a subtext. Which I take to mean a hidden message or import of some kind. So subtext, we know. But what do you call the message or meaning that’s right there on the surface? Completely open and obvious. They never talk about that. What do you call … what’s above the subtext?”
 “The text.”
 “Barcelona”, 1994. Share 2h ago 13.30 EST Preamble
 Aston Villa are three from three in the Champions League. Unai Emery’s side could top the league phase table outright after this evening’s meeting with Barcelona. But that is only part of the story.
 Emery returns to the Camp Nou – scene of one of his most traumatic nights as a manager – when in 2017 Barcelona overturned a 4-0 first-leg defeat by Paris Saint-Germain, winning 6-1 on the night , 6-5 on aggregate.
 So there would be subtext aplenty without the recent furore surrounding the pundit Jamie Carragher, Villa’s threatened legal action, Carragher’s apology , Villa dropping their legal threat … not to mention the fact that Emery has been linked with the Old Trafford managerial poisoned chalice hotseat amid Michael Carrick’s ongoing struggles .
 Throw in a disappointing week on the pitch for the Villains – an emphatic Carabao Cup by Bournemouth and a 1-1 draw with Fulham in the Premier League on Saturday – and it’s going to be fascinating to witness what transpires on the hallowed Camp Nou turf. Dani Olmo, Andreas Christensen, Eric García and Xavi Espart are expected to miss out for La Liga-leading Barça, while the forward Nicolas Jackson should be ready to go for Villa.
 Emery knows a thing or two about competing in European knockout competitions so regardless of subtexts and subplots, this should be a cracking game of association football. Vamos! 
 Kick-off: 8pm GMT
